overview: This file documents the condition of Japan’s canning and bottling industry during the early postwar occupation through two U.S. Political Adviser despatches. A December 1948 despatch encloses a detailed Hypothec Bank of Japan survey tracing the industry’s prewar expansion, wartime contraction, loss of colonial and northern fishing resources, postwar production and exports, shortages of tinplate and seasonings, financing problems, and proposals for consolidation and recovery. A September 1949 despatch supplies seven surviving statistical enclosures covering production and exports of canned marine products, fruits, vegetables, meat, and dairy products from 1937 through 1947; the expected fourth enclosure, on fruit exports, is absent from the supplied pages.

people.name: Matsuda
people.role: Founder or early pioneer of Japan’s canning industry, said to have learned oil-preservation of sardines from a Frenchman at Nagasaki in 1871

people.name: Kotaro Ono
people.role: Editor and publisher of HBJ Research Monthly, Foreign Department, Nippon Kan-gyo Bank, Ltd.

subfiles.title: Despatch No. 761 forwarding a report on Japan’s canning industry
subfiles.from: Acting Political Adviser for Japan, Tokyo
subfiles.about: Forwards a Hypothec Bank of Japan report describing the postwar condition and prospects of Japan’s canning industry.
subfiles.summary: The despatch refers to an earlier mission report on a national exhibition of Japanese canned goods and transmits five copies of a new industry survey. It reports that productive capacity had recovered to roughly half its 1939 level, while actual 1947 output was only 2.3 percent of the 1939 peak of approximately 18.29 million cases. Producers hoped that imported tinplate and seasonings would allow canned foods to regain their former importance in Japan’s export trade.

subfiles.title: Enclosure cover sheet for the canning-industry report
subfiles.from: United States Political Adviser for Japan
subfiles.about: Identifies the following report as the enclosure to Despatch No. 761.
subfiles.summary: This brief separator identifies the attached material as the enclosure to the Political Adviser’s December 4, 1948 despatch. It gives the subject as “Forwarding Report on Canning Industry in Japan.”

subfiles.title: HBJ Research Monthly No. 7: Canning Industry in Japan
subfiles.from: Hypothec Bank of Japan (Nippon Kan-gyo Bank, Ltd.)
subfiles.to: Foreign readers; enclosed for the U.S. Department of State
subfiles.about: Surveys the historical development, postwar condition, exports, material requirements, financing, and prospects of Japan’s canning and bottling industries.
subfiles.summary: The September–October 1948 report traces Japanese canning from Matsuda’s experiments at Nagasaki in 1871 through its rise into a major export industry whose 1939 production exceeded 18 million cases. It explains the collapse caused by wartime controls and the loss of Korea, Taiwan, Sakhalin, northern fishing grounds, and other sources of fish, fruit, and sugar. Detailed sections examine plant capacity, production and export statistics, regional and seasonal organization, diversification into other processed foods, exchange-rate competitiveness, shortages of tinplate and seasonings, and demands for ¥825 million in equipment and working funds. The report concludes that imported can materials, improved sanitation, and the rationalization and consolidation of factories could produce a partial recovery, although prewar prosperity was unlikely to return fully.

subfiles.title: Despatch No. 653 forwarding statistics on the Japanese canning industry
subfiles.from: Acting Political Adviser for Japan, Tokyo
subfiles.to: U.S. Department of State, for the Department of Commerce
subfiles.about: Forwards historical tables on Japanese canned-food production and exports for possible use by the Department of Commerce.
subfiles.summary: The despatch forwards eight categories of statistical tables on marine products, fruits, vegetables, meat, and dairy products, although only seven enclosure pages survive in this bundle. The tables were prepared by the Japanese canned-and-bottled-food trade association in response to an occupation-authorities inquiry and principally cover 1937–1947. The Economic and Scientific Section stated that subsequent canning statistics would appear in its monthly Japanese Economic Statistics.

subfiles.title: Production of canned marine products in Japan, 1937–1947
subfiles.from: Canned and Bottled Food Association of Japan
subfiles.to: Economic and Scientific Section, GHQ/SCAP; forwarded to the U.S. Department of State
subfiles.about: Tabulates annual Japanese production of major canned marine products from 1937 through 1947.
subfiles.summary: The table gives case totals for salmon, crabmeat, mackerel, abalone, sardines in tomato sauce, tuna, and other marine products. It shows the sharp decline from more than 7.7 million cases in 1937 to about 121,000 in 1947, while warning that wartime figures after 1941 are uncertain. A remark separately notes crabmeat and salmon packed in the Russian area in 1941.

subfiles.title: Exports of canned marine products from Japan
subfiles.from: Canned and Bottled Food Association of Japan
subfiles.to: Economic and Scientific Section, GHQ/SCAP; forwarded to the U.S. Department of State
subfiles.about: Tabulates Japanese exports of canned fish and shellfish during the late 1930s and early wartime years.
subfiles.summary: Although the OCR caption misreads the subject as canned meat, the listed commodities are salmon, crabmeat, mackerel, abalone, sardines, tuna, and other marine products. The table records very large prewar exports, especially of salmon and sardines in tomato sauce, followed by a steep contraction in 1940–1941. It states that figures for the subsequent wartime and immediate postwar period were unavailable.

subfiles.title: Production of canned fruits in Japan
subfiles.from: Canned and Bottled Food Association of Japan
subfiles.to: Economic and Scientific Section, GHQ/SCAP; forwarded to the U.S. Department of State
subfiles.about: Presents annual production figures for canned fruits before, during, and immediately after the Pacific War.
subfiles.summary: The table records canned-fruit output by variety from 1937 into the postwar period, though several commodity names are badly corrupted in the OCR. Its totals indicate rapid growth through 1939, followed by a severe wartime collapse and only limited recovery by 1946. Pineapple was the leading identifiable prewar category.

subfiles.title: Production of canned vegetables in Japan, 1937–1947
subfiles.from: Canned and Bottled Food Association of Japan
subfiles.to: Economic and Scientific Section, GHQ/SCAP; forwarded to the U.S. Department of State
subfiles.about: Tabulates production of Japanese canned vegetables by commodity from 1937 through 1947.
subfiles.summary: The enclosure covers fukujinzuke, asparagus, green peas, Japanese mushrooms, bamboo shoots, namako, burdock, beans, and other products, with some items divided by container size. It documents high prewar production, wartime contraction, and uneven postwar output across different vegetables.

subfiles.title: Exports of canned vegetables from Japan
subfiles.from: Canned and Bottled Food Association of Japan
subfiles.to: Economic and Scientific Section, GHQ/SCAP; forwarded to the U.S. Department of State
subfiles.about: Records Japanese exports of major canned vegetables in selected years from 1937 to 1947.
subfiles.summary: The table provides export figures for fukujinzuke, asparagus, green peas, Japanese mushrooms, bamboo shoots, burdock, beans, and other vegetables. Exports rose from about 214,000 cases in 1937 to roughly 531,000 in 1939, fell sharply in 1940, and totaled only about 8,000 cases in 1947. Bamboo shoots were the largest individually identified export category over the period.

subfiles.title: Production of canned meat and dairy products in Japan
subfiles.from: Canned and Bottled Food Association of Japan
subfiles.to: Economic and Scientific Section, GHQ/SCAP; forwarded to the U.S. Department of State
subfiles.about: Tabulates annual Japanese production of canned meat and sweetened condensed milk from 1937 through 1947.
subfiles.summary: The enclosure lists beef, beef with vegetables, pork, fowl and other meats, and sweetened condensed milk. Condensed milk dominated the category, while total production peaked in 1939 and declined drastically during the later war and immediate postwar years.

subfiles.title: Exports of canned meat and dairy products from Japan
subfiles.from: Canned and Bottled Food Association of Japan
subfiles.to: Economic and Scientific Section, GHQ/SCAP; forwarded to the U.S. Department of State
subfiles.about: Tabulates Japanese exports of canned meats and sweetened condensed milk for selected years between 1937 and 1947.
subfiles.summary: The table lists exports of beef, pork, fowl, other meats, and sweetened condensed milk. Condensed milk constituted the great majority of the recorded 973,327-case total. No 1947 exports are entered, illustrating the incompleteness of available postwar statistics.

interest: The file is valuable because it combines an interpretive occupation-era industry survey with commodity-level production and export tables spanning the transition from prewar expansion through wartime collapse and early reconstruction. It reveals how the loss of Japan’s empire and northern fisheries affected specific industries, while also documenting less visible constraints such as tinplate, sugar, seasonings, credit, exchange rates, sanitation requirements, and factory organization. The statistical enclosures permit direct comparison among marine, fruit, vegetable, meat, and dairy sectors, although historians must account for uncertain wartime figures, OCR-corrupted commodity names, inconsistent despatch numbers, and the absence of the expected enclosure on canned-fruit exports.
